witnesses.separates: Three 4 cells at three corners of a 1x2 box: $RectMarker reads them as a marker and draws a copy past its empty corner (11, 9); the concept, which reads only 2-apart square boxes, leaves them as they are.

Every marker spans a box whose corners are 3 apart: $DerivedStride derives stride 3 and draws a copy at the marker whose empty corner is (12, 5); the concept, at stride 2, finds no marker and so no template marker, and is undefined.

A template that is not symmetric about the diagonal through its marker's empty corner, and a marker whose empty corner (6, 10) is the top-right one: the concept mirrors the template across rows, and $Rotate turns it a quarter turn.
The template is drawn in 3: $AnyColorTemplate copies it in 3 at (11, 10); the concept, reading color 2, finds no template and is undefined.
The template holds 2 and 3 cells: $AnyColorTemplate copies both colors, and the concept copies only the 2 cells.
The markers are drawn in 3: $DerivedMarkerColor derives marker color 3 and draws a copy at (11, 10); the concept, reading color 4, finds no marker and is undefined.

The copies at (7, 5) and (5, 7) each cover a cell of the other's marker, (7, 7) and (5, 5), at a background cell of the template: the concept keeps those 4 cells, and $BoxStamp writes background over them.

The copy at the marker whose empty corner is (1, 11) runs one row past the top edge, and the concept draws the rows inside the grid. The 4 cells (1, 3), (1, 9) and (3, 9) also form a triple with corners 6 apart, whose empty corner is the template marker's, (3, 3): at the stored side bounds 6 to 8 the cells (1, 9) and (3, 9) lie in two triples, so $RectMarker & $DerivedMarkerColor finds no color whose cells split exactly and is undefined, while $RectMarker reads the same markers at every bound.

Two markers share column 0 of a 10x10 grid, so the 4 cells (0, 0), (0, 2), (6, 0) and (8, 0), (2, 0), (8, 2) also form triples with corners 6 apart: at the stored open side bounds 6 to 8 $RectMarker reads them as two more markers, the open bounds give different grids, and $RectMarker is undefined, while marker_max_side=SepTileCount gives bounds below 6 and draws the copy at (6, 2).
`background=DominantColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 0 and 1 swapped

Three markers hold nine 4 cells and the solid 4x4 template sixteen 2 cells, so the rarest color is the marker color: background=RarestColor drops 4 from the marker candidates and is undefined, while the stored background keeps 4 and the copies land at the empty corners (12, 5) and (12, 12).
`template_color=RarestColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 2 and 1 swapped

The input of stride-three, whose markers have corners 3 apart: marker_stride=TileCount gives the strides the 16-cell sides allow, 3 among them, and $DerivedMarkerColor finds color 4 splitting exactly at 3 and draws the copy at (12, 5); the stored stride 2 finds no marker.

Two markers share column 0 of a 10x10 grid, so the 4 cells (0, 0), (0, 2), (6, 0) and (8, 0), (2, 0), (8, 2) also form triples with corners 6 apart: at the stored open side bounds 6 to 8 $RectMarker reads them as two more markers, the open bounds give different grids, and $RectMarker is undefined, while marker_max_side=TileCount gives bounds below 6 and draws the copy at (6, 2).

Train 1 with 0 and 1 swapped, so the field is 1 and the template's bounding box holds 1 cells: $BoxStamp at the stored background writes 0 into them, and $BoxStamp & background=DominantColor writes 1, the concept's output.

Train 0 with 0 drawn as 1 and 4 drawn as 0, so the markers take the stored background's color: $DerivedMarkerColor at the stored background drops 0 from the marker candidates and is undefined, while background=DominantColor and background=RarestColor keep 0 and draw the copies.

A 5x5 template fills most of a 7x7 grid beside its one marker, so 2 is the commonest color: $AnyColorTemplate & background=DominantColor reads the 0 cells as the template, finds no marker at its box's corner and is undefined, while the stored background reads the 2 cells and gives the input back.

At marker_stride 5 and marker_max_side 5, markers with corners 5 apart on a 16x16 grid: the stored readings and $DerivedStride draw the copy at (9, 9), while marker_stride=TileCount and marker_max_side=TileCount read only the distances 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 the sides allow and are undefined.

A diagonal of 5 cells crosses every row and column, so no line is one color: marker_max_side=SepTileCount finds no separator lattice and is undefined, while marker_max_side=TileCount draws the copy at (8, 5); $AnyColorTemplate takes the diagonal into the template and is undefined, while template_color=RarestColor reads the 2 cells.

Train 2 with 0 and 1 swapped, and three 0 cells at (10, 20), (10, 22), (12, 20) forming a triple with corners 2 apart: $RectMarker reads 4 and draws the copies, while $DerivedMarkerColor & background=DominantColor finds both 0 and 4 splitting exactly and is undefined; background=RarestColor drops 0, the rarest color, and draws the copies.

Two markers share column 1, so the 4 cells (1, 1), (1, 3), (7, 1) and (9, 1), (3, 1), (9, 3) also form triples with corners 6 apart: at the stored side bounds 6 to 8, and at the bound 7 that marker_max_side=TileCount gives, $RectMarker reads them as two more markers whose copies write different colors to one cell, and is undefined, while marker_max_side=SepTileCount gives bounds below 6 and draws the copy at (7, 3).
